source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length1_42/training_1.csv"

df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

merged['timestamp'] = merged['timestamp'].astype(int)
merged['movie title'] = merged['movie title'].astype(str)

# Reorder columns to match target schema
Target1_42 = merged[['user_id', 'item_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'movie title']]

# Write the result to the specified path without the index
Target1_42.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on item_id
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1[['item_id', 'movie title']], on='item_id', how='inner')

# Group by user_id, item_id, movie title and aggregate rating and timestamp by max
# This is to enforce uniqueness and match the target key constraints
result = joined.groupby(['user_id', 'item_id', 'movie title'], as_index=False).agg({
    'rating': 'max',
    'timestamp': 'max'
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
result = result[['user_id', 'item_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'movie title']]

# Write to output CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
